answer: A sybil shield is per-epoch unique work graded by a rotating jury. Each identity must submit a fresh answer built from that epoch's three words, and the ledger rejects duplicates, so one script cannot mint a thousand clones from a single template. Each answer then enters a randomly drawn panel: a fake identity pays full compute and waiting time for one chance at a vote, and the panel can score it junk. Kinship weighting damps reciprocal vouching, so a farm gains little from backing its own clones. An honest newcomer still enters through a narrow inlet, calm as a zephyr or lantern in the dark.
